paper.title: The Slide Rule Guide: Ideas for If, When, and How to Use Generative AI Tools for Education

questions.theme: Generative AI tools as the new calculators
questions.prompt: In the essay's three-tool analogy, what do generative AI tools represent for the educational community?

choices.text: A new kind of paper-and-pencil exercise that builds foundational skills
The new calculators, which make some, but not all, existing approaches to teaching the equivalent of a slide rule
The new slide rules, which students should be steered away from
A temporary trend that will pass once students lose interest

questions.explanation: This probes the essay's central framing. Generative AI plays the role the calculator once did, and it turns some, but not all, existing activities into slide rules; the AI itself is not the slide rule.
questions.quote: For the educational community, I believe generative AI tools represent the new calculators that make some, but not all, of our existing approaches to learning and teaching the equivalent of a slide rule.

questions.theme: What makes an activity a slide rule
questions.prompt: Why, according to the essay, did many educational activities require labor-intensive steps before generative AI arrived?

choices.text: Because accreditation standards required a minimum amount of manual work
Because the steps themselves built essential understanding, like learning arithmetic by hand
Because there was no faster or more efficient way to obtain the result
Because students preferred hands-on work to using tools

questions.explanation: A slide-rule activity is one whose steps were required by the limits of available technology, not by their teaching value. Steps that build understanding are the paper-and-pencil case, which the essay treats separately.
questions.quote: not because the process itself was inherently valuable, but because there was no faster or more efficient way to obtain the result.

questions.prompt: Which of these does the essay give as examples of labor-intensive steps that students were required to perform? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Manually summarizing large bodies of text
Learning arithmetic by hand
Generating repetitive code structures
Composing boilerplate reports

questions.explanation: The essay names three kinds of labor-intensive work that existed because there was no faster method. Learning arithmetic by hand is its example of work that does build essential understanding.
questions.quote: These activities often required students to perform labor-intensive steps—such as manually summarizing large bodies of text, generating repetitive code structures, or composing boilerplate reports

questions.theme: The cost of keeping slide-rule activities
questions.prompt: Now that generative AI can handle such tasks in seconds, what does the essay say about still requiring students to do them the old way?

choices.text: It risks becoming the pedagogical equivalent of insisting they use a slide rule after calculators have become ubiquitous
It gives students the fundamentals they need for life after college
It is justified because AI output is usually lower in quality than student work
It should continue until AI tools become capable of doing these tasks

questions.explanation: The question tests the essay's argument for redesign. The tools already do these tasks quickly and often at a higher baseline quality, so keeping the old method is like keeping the slide rule after calculators are everywhere.
questions.quote: Today, with generative AI tools capable of handling these tasks in seconds and often at a higher baseline quality, continuing to require students to complete them in the old way risks becoming the pedagogical equivalent of insisting they use a slide rule after calculators have become ubiquitous.

questions.theme: Risk one: permitting AI where hand work is needed
questions.prompt: The first risk the essay names is permitting generative AI as a calculator when a pencil-and-paper approach is needed. What does that cost students?

choices.text: A slide rule when they need a calculator
The chance to produce work at a higher baseline quality
Access to the tools their future employers will expect them to use
The opportunity to learn fundamentals they need for life after college

questions.explanation: Over-permitting skips the hand work that builds fundamentals. Being handed a slide rule when a calculator is needed is the opposite risk, which comes from over-prohibiting.
questions.quote: We permit the use of these tools as calculators when we should require a pencil-and-paper approach, missing the opportunity for students to learn fundamentals that they need for life after college.

questions.theme: Risk two: prohibiting AI where it is appropriate
questions.prompt: What is the second risk the essay names?

choices.text: Permitting the tools when students should work by hand, so they miss fundamentals
Prohibiting the tools when they are appropriate, giving students a slide rule when they need a calculator
Using the tools to grade student work without reviewing the results
Teaching logarithms in place of practical computation

questions.explanation: The essay's risks run in both directions. The second is over-prohibiting: banning tools that would accelerate learning and make students more productive.
questions.quote: We prohibit these tools when they are appropriate for accelerating learning and making students more productive, giving them a slide rule when they need a calculator as a tool for life after college.

questions.prompt: The essay frames the educator's challenge as a distinction between two kinds of exercises. Which kind does it compare to learning arithmetic by hand?

choices.text: Exercises that are now obsolete workflows
Exercises that can be graded automatically
Exercises that build essential understanding
Exercises that generate repetitive code structures

questions.explanation: Arithmetic by hand stands for work worth keeping because it builds understanding. Obsolete workflows and repetitive code generation are the slide-rule side of the distinction.
questions.quote: Our challenge is to distinguish between exercises that build essential understanding—akin to learning arithmetic by hand—and those that are now obsolete workflows

questions.prompt: The essay says activities should be redesigned around which of the following? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Interpretation
Memorization
Creativity
Critical thinking
Manual repetition

questions.explanation: Once AI handles the slide-rule steps, the essay moves the instructional value to what students do with AI-generated output: interpret it, build on it creatively, and think critically about it.
questions.quote: The challenge is to distinguish these cases and redesign activities around interpretation, creativity, and critical thinking.
